objective: Produce the strongest hiring-useful portfolio language that is fully entailed by public-safe evidence, accurately attributes Jamie's role, preserves collective credit, and states uncertainty without shame or vagueness.

instructions: Make Jamie visible as an actor without claiming work performed by collaborators.
Describe emerging conditions as normal features of transition, not organizational failure.
Name what became usable and why it mattered to the intended reader.
Use only evidence supplied in the fixture or an approved Knowledge Bank record.
Treat every output as public and quotable.

hardGates.description: Every consequential factual claim is directly supported by the supplied evidence at the stated precision.
hardGates.passCondition: The evaluator can map each consequential clause to evidence without adding assumptions or broadening a source.
failureExamples: Turning a recovered account interaction into institutional endorsement
Presenting a current engagement counter as contemporaneous impact
Converting not recovered into never existed

hardGates.description: Jamie's work, collaborator work, account-level actions, and institutional actions remain distinct.
hardGates.passCondition: Actor, action, and scope are explicit, and the copy does not silently move credit between people, accounts, teams, or institutions.
failureExamples: Saying Jamie led a collective campaign when the evidence supports web infrastructure
Saying an elected member personally authored a post when only account-level evidence exists
Treating a tagged account as an engaged account

hardGates.description: Known, open, reconstructed, and protected material remain distinguishable.
hardGates.passCondition: Coverage gaps and source limits are stated at the level needed to prevent a reasonable reader from drawing a stronger conclusion.
failureExamples: Calling a 107-of-110 recovery complete
Omitting that surviving social counters can change
Using cautious language so broadly that supported facts become illegible

hardGates.description: The copy claims Jamie's documented contribution while preserving the agency and credit of collaborators.
hardGates.passCondition: Direct authorship is direct, collective accomplishments are collective, and contribution language is used where causality is shared.
failureExamples: Replacing direct authorship with vague passive voice
Claiming sole ownership of a collective outcome
Erasing named public organizers or team members

hardGates.description: The candidate is safe for a public repository and newspaper quotation.
hardGates.passCondition: No private path, raw correspondence, protected identity, credential, private metric, or unapproved source artifact appears.
failureExamples: Publishing a local filesystem path
Quoting a private transcript
Exposing participant identities or source metadata beyond approval

hardGates.description: Public copy does not exceed the strongest approved Knowledge Bank claim or its allowed surface.
hardGates.passCondition: Any stronger wording is proposed as a bank update with evidence and guardrails before it is projected publicly.
failureExamples: Strengthening website copy while leaving the claim register weaker
Publishing a pending or internal-only claim
Dropping an archived, unofficial, contribution, or collective-work guardrail

hardGates.description: Emergence and ambiguity are framed as normal conditions of change rather than sources of shame.
hardGates.passCondition: The copy offers agency and structure without describing collaborators as confused, dysfunctional, or deficient.
failureExamples: Teams that cannot get organized
Fixing chaotic stakeholders
Rescuing organizations from their own confusion

hardGates.description: Photographs are treated as corroboration of visible presence, settings, artifacts, and material continuity rather than self-authenticating proof or publication consent.
hardGates.passCondition: The candidate distinguishes visible observation, retrieval hypothesis, documentary claim, and asset-specific publication approval without transferring certainty between them.
failureExamples: Treating a People association as identity confirmation, consent, or professional role
Treating project-album membership as proof of authorship, leadership, or outcome
Calling every editor-field candidate approved for publication
Converting attribution not established in this run into the work did not happen

anchors.1: The reader cannot tell what Jamie does or why it matters.
anchors.3: The role is understandable but abstract, crowded, or slow to parse.
anchors.5: A hiring reader can identify Jamie's role, value, and fit in one pass.

anchors.1: Uses abstractions or passive voice without a legible contribution.
anchors.3: Names an action but leaves the resulting usable change vague.
anchors.5: Clearly connects Jamie's bounded action to what became usable and for whom.

anchors.1: Relies on generic competence language or unsupported superlatives.
anchors.3: Includes some concrete detail but misses the strongest defensible proof.
anchors.5: Uses the most decision-relevant supported detail without evidentiary clutter.

anchors.1: Materially overstates, understates, or blurs the evidence boundary.
anchors.3: Technically careful but either timid or insufficiently bounded.
anchors.5: Claims the full supported record and no more, with proportionate limits.

anchors.1: Requires rereading, domain knowledge, or interpretation to find the point.
anchors.3: Mostly clear but carries avoidable clauses, jargon, or caveats.
anchors.5: Sequences claim, value, and limit with minimal cognitive load.

anchors.1: Sounds inflated, clinical, ashamed, or generic.
anchors.3: Competent and accurate but interchangeable with ordinary portfolio copy.
anchors.5: Precise, warm, grounded, and quietly confident without becoming poetic fog.

anchors.1: Reads as an isolated anecdote with no role relevance.
anchors.3: Suggests a capability but leaves the future-use case implicit.
anchors.5: Makes the demonstrated capability legible in the reader's likely environment.

requiredOutput.hardGates: Object keyed by gate ID with pass, evidence, and correction fields.
requiredOutput.scores: Object keyed by scored criterion ID with integer score from 1 to 5 and a short rationale.
requiredOutput.regressions: List of ways the candidate is worse than the previous accepted candidate.
requiredOutput.revisionBrief: Smallest set of changes likely to improve the score without weakening a passed gate.

rules: Judge only against the supplied evidence pack and rubric.
Do not reward rhetorical force when it reduces calibration.
Compare candidates blind to author and iteration number.
A failed hard gate always produces block, regardless of weighted score.
The generator may not score its own candidate as the deciding judge.

stopPolicy.selectionRule: Keep the highest-scoring candidate that passes every hard gate. Never replace it with a louder candidate that introduces a regression.
stopPolicy.successCondition: Both independent judges pass every hard gate, weighted score is at least 92, every criterion is at least 4, calibration is 5, and the result passes twice consecutively.
stopPolicy.failureCondition: If the criterion is not reached by iteration 8 or two accepted-draft regressions occur, return the best passing candidate with unresolved criteria and do not label the run complete.

loop: Load one fixture, its public-safe evidence, and the current accepted candidate.
Run deterministic public-safety and forbidden-claim checks.
Have the evidence judge evaluate entailment, attribution, uncertainty, and boundaries.
Have the hiring-reader judge evaluate clarity, reader burden, voice, and transferable value.
Reject any candidate that fails a hard gate or regresses from the accepted candidate.
Give the generator only the judges' bounded revision brief, not hidden expected answers.
Revise the smallest necessary span and evaluate again.
Stop only under the success or failure condition in stopPolicy.
